en: I praise the Lord, the Master of life, the All-pervading One, the Lord of the universe, the Lord of the lords of the world, the eternal possessor of bliss, the Sovereign of the past, present, and future, the Lord of beings, Śiva, Śaṅkara, Śambhu, and Īśāna. || 1 ||

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, and Īśāna, who wears a garland of skulls around his neck, a mass of serpents upon his body, who is the death of even Mahākāla, who is the lord of the Gaṇas, and who is distinguished by the waves of the Gaṅgā flowing through his matted locks.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Lord Īśāna—the mine of joy, the ornament adorning the great circle (of the universe), wearing ashes as his decoration, beginningless, boundless, the great destroyer of delusion. || 3 ||
I praise the one who dwells beneath the banyan tree, whose great laughter is loud, who destroys great sins, and who is ever brilliantly radiant;
I praise Giriśa, Gaṇeśa, Sureśa, Maheśa, Śiva, Śaṅkara, Śambhu, and Īśāna.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Lord, the Supreme Brahman who is worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods; he whose body and purpose are ever grasped by the Daughter of the Mountain King, who dwells eternally on the mountain, and whose abode is the eternal mountain.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, Īśāna— the foremost among the gods who ride upon the bull— who holds a skull and a trident in his two hands and bestows all desires upon those who bow at his lotus feet.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, and Īśāna— whose body is like the autumnal moon, who is the vessel of joy for his attendants, who possesses three eyes, who is the friend of the Lord of Wealth, whose wife is Aparṇā, and whose conduct is ever virtuous.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Lord Īśāna— who wears a serpent as a necklace, who sports upon the ground of the funeral pyre, who is the essence of the Vedas, who is eternally changeless, who dwells in the cremation ground, and who consumes the god of love (Manoja).

The man who himself recites this Jewel of a Hymn to the Trident-Bearer at dawn, having obtained the jewel in this world, shall—having propitiated Him with various offerings along with his sons, excellent grain, friends, and wife—attain liberation. (This is the declaration of the fruit.)
